title: Chapter 112 — Scheduling, Communication & The Operating Cadence
intro: Staffing logic, communication systems, and the store's rhythms.

sections.title: Staff to Traffic
sections.content:
The most expensive mistake a store manager makes is having 6 reps on a Tuesday morning and 2 on a Saturday afternoon. Staff to traffic, not to preference.

Monday-Tuesday: lowest traffic. Good for follow-ups and training. Wednesday-Thursday: moderate, good for trade appointments. Friday: picks up afternoon and evening. Saturday: highest traffic day — all hands, no days off. Sunday: moderate to high with promotions.

Peak hours — Saturday 10am-4pm — need maximum coverage. Manager on the floor, not in the office. Off-peak — weekday mornings — minimum coverage. This is training time and pipeline time.

sections.title: The Communication System
sections.content:
Daily huddle: five minutes before doors open. Wins, focus for the day, one product fact, numbers against goal, energy. Weekly team meeting: 30 minutes. Review the week, preview the next, training segment, recognition.

The shift handoff: when shifts overlap, the outgoing rep briefs the incoming rep on pending customers, delivery issues, and open situations. Nothing should fall through the crack between shifts.

sections.title: The Operating Cadence
sections.content:
Great stores have a rhythm. Daily huddle. Daily Five calls. Midday floor check. End-of-day review. Weekly team meeting. Weekly one-on-ones. Monthly scorecards. Quarterly business reviews.

This cadence creates predictability. Everyone knows what to expect. Everyone knows the standards. Everyone knows how they are performing. The cadence is the operating system of the store — and it runs whether the manager is present or not.
